text: With scope locked, the first architecture decision is the platform itself -- and the honest answer isn't more logins. It's a governed Databricks Lakehouse on Unity Catalog.

One catalog, harborview, with three schemas: claims_raw lands nightly CSV drops through Auto Loader; claims_clean applies a quality check with a Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline; two gold tables split the audience -- one clinic-level, one patient-level.

More shared logins, hand-maintained view permissions, filtering inside a dashboard -- all rejected. None of them give a real audit trail, and all of them can quietly drift out of sync with the policy.
Unity Catalog enforces the policy at the platform level instead -- tied to who someone actually is, not which login they happened to share.
The stack is chosen. Next: turning this plan into an actual medallion schema.
